title_en: Building World Models from Intrinsic Motivation
title_zh: 从内在动机构建世界模型
summary_en: This study integrates 24 intrinsic objectives (curiosity, entropy, competency) into a model-based RL framework to learn world models without extrinsic rewards. Using three representation-learning strategies (observation reconstruction, latent prediction, redundancy reduction), they evaluate zero-shot, few-shot, and multi-task control in locomotion, manipulation, and open-ended games. Curiosity-driven exploration with observation reconstruction yields the strongest aggregate profile, though the best individual pairing is task-dependent. In compositional vision tasks, intrinsic motivation from episodic and lifelong novelty—complementing the world model's recurrent state—achieves the best zero-shot transfer and few-shot performance.
summary_zh: 本研究将24种内在动机目标（好奇心、熵、能力）集成到基于模型的强化学习框架中，以在无外部奖励下学习世界模型。采用三种表示学习策略（观测重建、潜在预测、冗余减少），在运动、操作和开放式游戏中评估零样本、少样本和多任务控制。好奇心驱动探索结合观测重建获得最强的综合表现，但最佳个体组合取决于任务。在组合视觉任务中，来自情景和终身新颖性的内在动机——作为世界模型通用循环状态的补充记忆——实现了最佳的零样本迁移和少样本性能。
content_en: In the absence of extrinsic rewards or task supervision, human behavior is guided by intrinsic motivation---neural signals that drive curiosity, creativity, play, and other essential facets of intelligence. Intrinsic motivation plays an important developmental role in building robust world models that enable generalization and adaptation. Yet existing studies leave open how a broad range of intrinsic motivations interacts with world-model representation learning to support downstream control. This limits our understanding of which intrinsically collected experiences build reusable models. To address these gaps, we integrate 24 intrinsic objectives, including established methods and explicit variants spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency, into a common model-based reinforcement learning framework. We evaluate the world models they build through zero-shot, few-shot, and multi-task control in locomotion, manipulation, and open-ended gaming environments, using three representation-learning strategies: observation reconstruction, latent prediction, and redundancy reduction. Curiosity-driven exploration with observation reconstruction yields the strongest aggregate family profile, although the best individual pairing depends on the experiment. content_zh: 在缺乏外在奖励或任务监督的情况下，人类行为由内在动机引导——即驱动好奇心、创造力、玩耍以及其他智能基本要素的神经信号。内在动机在构建稳健的世界模型方面发挥着重要的发展性作用，这些模型能够实现泛化与适应。然而，现有研究尚未阐明广泛的内在动机如何与世界模型表征学习相互作用以支持下游控制。这限制了我们对哪些内在收集的经验能够构建可复用模型的理解。为填补这些空白，我们将24种内在目标——包括已有方法以及涵盖好奇心、熵和胜任力的显式变体——集成到一个共同的基于模型的强化学习框架中。我们通过零样本、少样本和多任务控制在运动、操作和开放式游戏环境中评估它们所构建的世界模型，并采用三种表征学习策略：观测重建、潜在预测和冗余缩减。以观测重建为基础的好奇心驱动探索在总体上产生了最强的家族画像，尽管最佳个体配对取决于具体实验。在组合式视觉任务中，源自情节性和终身新颖性的内在动机——为世界模型的通用循环状态提供互补记忆——实现了最佳的零样本迁移和少样本
